title: In Hilbert space, all things are quantumly possible
title_zh: 在希尔伯特空间中，一切皆有可能（量子层面）

paragraphs.en: Quantum objects have multiple possible futures before they are observed. Hilbert space allows physicists to explore those possibilities.
paragraphs.zh: 量子物体在被观测之前拥有多种可能的未来。 希尔伯特空间使物理学家能够探索这些可能性。

sents.en: Quantum objects have multiple possible futures before they are observed.
sents.zh: 量子物体在被观测之前拥有多种可能的未来。

sents.en: Hilbert space allows physicists to explore those possibilities.
sents.zh: 希尔伯特空间使物理学家能够探索这些可能性。

paragraphs.en: A t the heart of quantum mechanics lie a few sacred rules for how to use the theory. First and foremost is, roughly, that thou shalt not think about ordinary objects presently whizzing through ordinary space. Rather, quantum mechanics predicts — in exquisite detail — all the possible ways that an object might turn out to be in the future. Exploring those possible futures requires tracking an entirely different mathematical object — an arrow known as a vector, one oriented in an expansive, alien domain.
paragraphs.zh: 量子力学核心处存在着几条关于如何使用这一理论的神圣规则。 首要的一条大致是：不可去思考那些正在普通空间中飞驰的普通物体。 相反，量子力学以极其精妙的方式预测一个物体在未来可能呈现的一切情形。 探索这些可能的未来需要追踪一个完全不同的数学对象——一个被称为向量的箭头，它指向一个广阔而陌生的领域。

sents.en: A t the heart of quantum mechanics lie a few sacred rules for how to use the theory.
sents.zh: 量子力学核心处存在着几条关于如何使用这一理论的神圣规则。

sents.en: First and foremost is, roughly, that thou shalt not think about ordinary objects presently whizzing through ordinary space.
sents.zh: 首要的一条大致是：不可去思考那些正在普通空间中飞驰的普通物体。

sents.en: Rather, quantum mechanics predicts — in exquisite detail — all the possible ways that an object might turn out to be in the future.
sents.zh: 相反，量子力学以极其精妙的方式预测一个物体在未来可能呈现的一切情形。

sents.en: Exploring those possible futures requires tracking an entirely different mathematical object — an arrow known as a vector, one oriented in an expansive, alien domain.
sents.zh: 探索这些可能的未来需要追踪一个完全不同的数学对象——一个被称为向量的箭头，它指向一个广阔而陌生的领域。

paragraphs.en: These arrows aren’t pointing at locations. “It’s a much more abstract space than that,” said Lucien Hardy , a physicist at the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics in Waterloo, Canada. They’re “really pointing in a direction in a possibility space.”
paragraphs.zh: 这些箭头并不是指向各个地点。“这是一个比那抽象得多的空间，”加拿大滑铁卢圆周理论物理研究所的物理学家吕西安·哈迪说。 它们“实际上指向的是可能性空间中的某个方向。”

sents.en: These arrows aren’t pointing at locations. “It’s a much more abstract space than that,” said Lucien Hardy , a physicist at the Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics in Waterloo, Canada.
sents.zh: 这些箭头并不是指向各个地点。“这是一个比那抽象得多的空间，”加拿大滑铁卢圆周理论物理研究所的物理学家吕西安·哈迪说。

sents.en: They’re “really pointing in a direction in a possibility space.”
sents.zh: 它们“实际上指向的是可能性空间中的某个方向。”

paragraphs.en: This possibility space is called Hilbert space, and it acts as the primary arena for quantum physics.
paragraphs.zh: 这个可能性空间被称为希尔伯特空间，它充当着量子物理学的主要舞台。

paragraphs.en: The early quantum pioneers didn’t realize — at first — that the arcane math that strikingly captured the conduct of atoms had left the real world behind. It took a visionary mathematical physicist, John von Neumann, to recognize and define the quantum world as a Hilbert space. Once he did, exploring the ins and outs of Hilbert space would lead physicists to a deeper, more unified understanding of quantum physics.
paragraphs.zh: 早期的量子先驱们起初并没有意识到，那套精妙地刻画了原子行为的晦涩数学其实早已脱离了现实世界。 直到富有远见的数学物理学家约翰·冯·诺依曼（John von Neumann）认识到并把量子世界定义为希尔伯特空间，情况才有所改变。 一旦他做到了这一点，对希尔伯特空间来龙去脉的探索便会引导物理学家对量子物理学获得更深刻、更统一的理解。

sents.en: The early quantum pioneers didn’t realize — at first — that the arcane math that strikingly captured the conduct of atoms had left the real world behind.
sents.zh: 早期的量子先驱们起初并没有意识到，那套精妙地刻画了原子行为的晦涩数学其实早已脱离了现实世界。

sents.en: It took a visionary mathematical physicist, John von Neumann, to recognize and define the quantum world as a Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 直到富有远见的数学物理学家约翰·冯·诺依曼（John von Neumann）认识到并把量子世界定义为希尔伯特空间，情况才有所改变。

sents.en: Once he did, exploring the ins and outs of Hilbert space would lead physicists to a deeper, more unified understanding of quantum physics.
sents.zh: 一旦他做到了这一点，对希尔伯特空间来龙去脉的探索便会引导物理学家对量子物理学获得更深刻、更统一的理解。

paragraphs.en: Here’s how von Neumann’s first commandment of quantum physics came to be, and how to understand it.
paragraphs.zh: 以下是冯·诺依曼的量子物理学第一诫命是如何产生的，以及如何理解它。

paragraphs.en: Von Neumann’s commandments, or axioms, were his way of making sense of the two distinct forms of quantum mechanics developed back-to-back in the 1920s. First came Werner Heisenberg’s “matrix mechanics” in 1925. It used inscrutable tables and, in later formulations, interminable towers of numbers to calculate the odds that an electron circling an atom would jump to a higher or lower orbit. The next year, Erwin Schrödinger introduced his “wave mechanics.” It used waves to track, for instance, the probability of a particle being found at a certain location in space. While the pictures evoked by these two physicists looked completely distinct, they yielded identical predictions. Heisenberg and Schrödinger had come up with two radically different incarnations of one theory. But what was that theory?
paragraphs.zh: 冯·诺依曼的戒律，或者说公理，是他用来理解20世纪20年代相继出现的两种不同形式量子力学的方式。 首先登场的是维尔纳·海森堡1925年提出的“矩阵力学”。 它使用晦涩难懂的表格，以及在后来的表述中绵延无尽的数字高塔，来计算绕原子运转的电子跃迁到更高或更低轨道的概率。 次年，埃尔温·薛定谔提出了他的“波动力学”。它用波来追踪诸如粒子在空间中某处被发现的概率。 尽管这两位物理学家所唤起的图景看起来截然不同，但它们给出的预测却完全一致。 海森堡和薛定谔提出了同一理论的两种截然不同的化身。 但那个理论究竟是什么？

sents.en: Von Neumann’s commandments, or axioms, were his way of making sense of the two distinct forms of quantum mechanics developed back-to-back in the 1920s.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼的戒律，或者说公理，是他用来理解20世纪20年代相继出现的两种不同形式量子力学的方式。

sents.en: First came Werner Heisenberg’s “matrix mechanics” in 1925.
sents.zh: 首先登场的是维尔纳·海森堡1925年提出的“矩阵力学”。

sents.en: It used inscrutable tables and, in later formulations, interminable towers of numbers to calculate the odds that an electron circling an atom would jump to a higher or lower orbit.
sents.zh: 它使用晦涩难懂的表格，以及在后来的表述中绵延无尽的数字高塔，来计算绕原子运转的电子跃迁到更高或更低轨道的概率。

sents.en: The next year, Erwin Schrödinger introduced his “wave mechanics.” It used waves to track, for instance, the probability of a particle being found at a certain location in space.
sents.zh: 次年，埃尔温·薛定谔提出了他的“波动力学”。它用波来追踪诸如粒子在空间中某处被发现的概率。

sents.en: While the pictures evoked by these two physicists looked completely distinct, they yielded identical predictions.
sents.zh: 尽管这两位物理学家所唤起的图景看起来截然不同，但它们给出的预测却完全一致。

sents.en: Heisenberg and Schrödinger had come up with two radically different incarnations of one theory.
sents.zh: 海森堡和薛定谔提出了同一理论的两种截然不同的化身。

sents.en: But what was that theory?
sents.zh: 但那个理论究竟是什么？

paragraphs.en: The question fascinated David Hilbert, a renowned mathematician who had devoted much of his life to rebuilding physics on a sturdy foundation of crisp axioms. He got von Neumann thinking about the problem in the mid-1920s. In 1927 the 23-year-old prodigy — building on insights from Paul Dirac — solved it in a single-author trilogy of papers .
paragraphs.zh: 这个问题令大卫·希尔伯特着迷，他是一位著名数学家，一生中的大量精力都奉献给了以清晰公理的坚实根基重建物理学的事业。 他在 20 世纪 20 年代中期让冯·诺依曼开始思考这个问题。 1927 年，这位 23 岁的天才——在保罗·狄拉克的洞见基础上——以一组单人署名的三联篇论文解决了这个问题。

sents.en: The question fascinated David Hilbert, a renowned mathematician who had devoted much of his life to rebuilding physics on a sturdy foundation of crisp axioms.
sents.zh: 这个问题令大卫·希尔伯特着迷，他是一位著名数学家，一生中的大量精力都奉献给了以清晰公理的坚实根基重建物理学的事业。

sents.en: He got von Neumann thinking about the problem in the mid-1920s.
sents.zh: 他在 20 世纪 20 年代中期让冯·诺依曼开始思考这个问题。

sents.en: In 1927 the 23-year-old prodigy — building on insights from Paul Dirac — solved it in a single-author trilogy of papers .
sents.zh: 1927 年，这位 23 岁的天才——在保罗·狄拉克的洞见基础上——以一组单人署名的三联篇论文解决了这个问题。

paragraphs.en: The mathematician David Hilbert sought a mathematical structure that would unify the different forms of quantum mechanics.
paragraphs.zh: 数学家大卫·希尔伯特（David Hilbert）试图寻找一种能够统一量子力学不同形式的数学结构。

paragraphs.en: “The ideas specifically were von Neumann’s, but the inspiration — why do you axiomatize and what for — this is something that he took from Hilbert,” said Leo Corry , a historian of mathematics.
paragraphs.zh: “具体的思想是冯·诺依曼的，但灵感——你为什么要公理化、公理化是为了什么——这些是他从希尔伯特那里得来的，”数学史学家利奥·科里说。

paragraphs.en: These papers laid out the rules for quantum mechanics, carefully defining the theory’s central objects and how they behaved. Von Neumann showed that Heisenberg’s towers and Schrödinger’s waves were reflections of the same entity, just as 0.5 and ½ indicate the same point on the number line. They both represented the main character in quantum mechanics: the quantum state.
paragraphs.zh: 这些论文为量子力学制定了规则，仔细定义了该理论的核心对象及其行为方式。 冯·诺依曼证明了海森堡的矩阵和薛定谔的波是同一实体的不同映像，正如 0.5 和 ½ 表示数轴上的同一个点。 它们都代表了量子力学中的主角：量子态。

sents.en: These papers laid out the rules for quantum mechanics, carefully defining the theory’s central objects and how they behaved.
sents.zh: 这些论文为量子力学制定了规则，仔细定义了该理论的核心对象及其行为方式。

sents.en: Von Neumann showed that Heisenberg’s towers and Schrödinger’s waves were reflections of the same entity, just as 0.5 and ½ indicate the same point on the number line.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼证明了海森堡的矩阵和薛定谔的波是同一实体的不同映像，正如 0.5 和 ½ 表示数轴上的同一个点。

sents.en: They both represented the main character in quantum mechanics: the quantum state.
sents.zh: 它们都代表了量子力学中的主角：量子态。

paragraphs.en: Everything has a state. A coin can read heads or tails. A grandfather clock’s bob can take on any number of positions as it swings. Most of physics amounts to capturing an object’s state and predicting how it will change.
paragraphs.zh: 万物皆有状态。 一枚硬币可以读出正面或反面。 落地钟的钟摆在摆动时可以处于任意多个位置。 大部分物理学的内容，本质上就是捕捉一个物体的状态，并预测它将如何变化。

sents.en: Everything has a state.
sents.zh: 万物皆有状态。

sents.en: A coin can read heads or tails.
sents.zh: 一枚硬币可以读出正面或反面。

sents.en: A grandfather clock’s bob can take on any number of positions as it swings.
sents.zh: 落地钟的钟摆在摆动时可以处于任意多个位置。

sents.en: Most of physics amounts to capturing an object’s state and predicting how it will change.
sents.zh: 大部分物理学的内容，本质上就是捕捉一个物体的状态，并预测它将如何变化。

paragraphs.en: Von Neumann’s quantum rules complicate the notion of a state. Before you observe a quantum object, it does not have a fixed set of properties, such as a specific position. Instead it has a combination of possible properties unique to quantum mechanics — a “quantum superposition.” A superposition combines, for instance, all possible places the particle might end up being. Those possibilities can be precise and informative; perhaps there is a 99% chance you’ll find your particle to your left and a 1% chance you’ll find it to your right. You know how to place your bets, but you can’t know for sure if you’ve won until you check.
paragraphs.zh: 冯·诺依曼的量子规则使“态”这一概念变得复杂。 在你观测一个量子对象之前，它并不具有一组固定的属性，比如某个具体的位置。 相反，它具有一种量子力学独有的、各种可能属性的叠加态——即“量子叠加态”。例如，叠加态包含了粒子最终可能处于的所有位置。 这些可能性可以精确且信息丰富；也许你有 99% 的概率会发现粒子在你的左边，1% 的概率会发现它在你的右边。 你知道该如何下注，但在查验之前，你无法确定自己是否赢了。

sents.en: Von Neumann’s quantum rules complicate the notion of a state.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼的量子规则使“态”这一概念变得复杂。

sents.en: Before you observe a quantum object, it does not have a fixed set of properties, such as a specific position.
sents.zh: 在你观测一个量子对象之前，它并不具有一组固定的属性，比如某个具体的位置。

sents.en: Instead it has a combination of possible properties unique to quantum mechanics — a “quantum superposition.” A superposition combines, for instance, all possible places the particle might end up being.
sents.zh: 相反，它具有一种量子力学独有的、各种可能属性的叠加态——即“量子叠加态”。例如，叠加态包含了粒子最终可能处于的所有位置。

sents.en: Those possibilities can be precise and informative; perhaps there is a 99% chance you’ll find your particle to your left and a 1% chance you’ll find it to your right.
sents.zh: 这些可能性可以精确且信息丰富；也许你有 99% 的概率会发现粒子在你的左边，1% 的概率会发现它在你的右边。

sents.zh: 你知道该如何下注，但在查验之前，你无法确定自己是否赢了。

paragraphs.en: Von Neumann rendered the quantum state as a mathematical arrow called a vector. This arrow points in some direction through a space capturing all the possible futures of any quantum object — a Hilbert space.
paragraphs.zh: 冯·诺依曼将量子态表示为一个称为向量的数学箭头。 这个箭头穿过一个空间指向某个方向，该空间涵盖了任何量子客体的所有可能未来——即希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: Von Neumann rendered the quantum state as a mathematical arrow called a vector.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼将量子态表示为一个称为向量的数学箭头。

sents.en: This arrow points in some direction through a space capturing all the possible futures of any quantum object — a Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 这个箭头穿过一个空间指向某个方向，该空间涵盖了任何量子客体的所有可能未来——即希尔伯特空间。

paragraphs.en: Imagine a quantum traffic light with three possible states — red, yellow, or green. Its arrow exists in a three-dimensional Hilbert space, where the three axes represent the three possible future colors. Until the moment the light is observed, it doesn’t have a color, but rather a mixture of possible colors. So its arrow points into the space’s central region. The more closely the arrow aligns with, say, the red axis, the more likely the light is to shine red.
paragraphs.zh: 想象一个有三种可能状态的红绿灯——红灯、黄灯或绿灯。 它的箭头存在于一个三维希尔伯特空间中，其中三条坐标轴代表三种可能的未来颜色。 在被观测到的那一刻之前，这盏灯并没有颜色，而是各种可能颜色的混合。 因此它的箭头指向空间的中心区域。 箭头与某条轴（比如说红色轴）对齐得越紧，这盏灯亮红色的可能性就越大。

sents.en: Imagine a quantum traffic light with three possible states — red, yellow, or green.
sents.zh: 想象一个有三种可能状态的红绿灯——红灯、黄灯或绿灯。

sents.en: Its arrow exists in a three-dimensional Hilbert space, where the three axes represent the three possible future colors.
sents.zh: 它的箭头存在于一个三维希尔伯特空间中，其中三条坐标轴代表三种可能的未来颜色。

sents.en: Until the moment the light is observed, it doesn’t have a color, but rather a mixture of possible colors.
sents.zh: 在被观测到的那一刻之前，这盏灯并没有颜色，而是各种可能颜色的混合。

sents.en: So its arrow points into the space’s central region.
sents.zh: 因此它的箭头指向空间的中心区域。

sents.en: The more closely the arrow aligns with, say, the red axis, the more likely the light is to shine red.
sents.zh: 箭头与某条轴（比如说红色轴）对齐得越紧，这盏灯亮红色的可能性就越大。

paragraphs.en: The state of any object, from an electron to a galaxy, can be captured by such a vector, pointing in some direction through such a Hilbert space. This is von Neumann’s first rule of quantum mechanics.
paragraphs.zh: 任何对象的状态，从电子到星系，都可以用这样一个向量来描述，该向量在这个希尔伯特空间中指向某个方向。 这就是冯·诺依曼的量子力学第一规则。

sents.en: The state of any object, from an electron to a galaxy, can be captured by such a vector, pointing in some direction through such a Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 任何对象的状态，从电子到星系，都可以用这样一个向量来描述，该向量在这个希尔伯特空间中指向某个方向。

sents.en: This is von Neumann’s first rule of quantum mechanics.
sents.zh: 这就是冯·诺依曼的量子力学第一规则。

paragraphs.en: An arrow moves through Hilbert space in one of two ways. Von Neumann’s other commandments specify how.
paragraphs.zh: 一个箭头以两种方式之一在希尔伯特空间中移动。 冯·诺依曼的另一些戒律规定了它是如何移动的。

sents.en: An arrow moves through Hilbert space in one of two ways.
sents.zh: 一个箭头以两种方式之一在希尔伯特空间中移动。

sents.en: Von Neumann’s other commandments specify how.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼的另一些戒律规定了它是如何移动的。

paragraphs.en: The first possibility corresponds to what happens before an observation. As the world influences the object, changing its state, the arrow turns smoothly through Hilbert space. It might get closer to the green axis, which would make our traffic light more likely to be measured as green, or to red or yellow. The point is that all this happens smoothly and predictably.
paragraphs.zh: 第一种可能性对应的是一次观测之前所发生的情况。 当世界影响这个物体、改变其状态时，箭头会在希尔伯特空间中平滑地转动。 它可能更靠近绿色轴，这会让我们红绿灯被测为绿色的可能性更大，或者靠近红色轴或黄色轴。 关键在于，这一切都平滑且可预测地发生。

sents.en: The first possibility corresponds to what happens before an observation.
sents.zh: 第一种可能性对应的是一次观测之前所发生的情况。

sents.en: As the world influences the object, changing its state, the arrow turns smoothly through Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 当世界影响这个物体、改变其状态时，箭头会在希尔伯特空间中平滑地转动。

sents.en: It might get closer to the green axis, which would make our traffic light more likely to be measured as green, or to red or yellow.
sents.zh: 它可能更靠近绿色轴，这会让我们红绿灯被测为绿色的可能性更大，或者靠近红色轴或黄色轴。

sents.en: The point is that all this happens smoothly and predictably.
sents.zh: 关键在于，这一切都平滑且可预测地发生。

paragraphs.en: Then, if you actually observe the system, the vector will instantly and randomly snap onto either the red, yellow, or green axis. The more aligned it is with one axis, the more likely it is to snap to that axis instead of the others, but its fate is ultimately unpredictable. Let’s say it goes green. You’ll observe a green light, and there is now a 100% chance that it will still be green in subsequent measurements, because the arrow is fully aligned with the green axis. The quantum superposition is no more.
paragraphs.zh: 然后，如果你真的对这个系统进行观测，这个向量会瞬间随机地跳变到红色、黄色或绿色轴中的某一条上。 它与某条轴越对齐，就越有可能跳变到那条轴而不是其他轴，但它的最终归宿是不可预测的。假设它跳到了绿色。 你会观测到绿光，并且此后再测量它仍是绿色的概率为100%，因为这个箭头已经完全与绿色轴对齐。 量子叠加态不复存在。

sents.en: Then, if you actually observe the system, the vector will instantly and randomly snap onto either the red, yellow, or green axis.
sents.zh: 然后，如果你真的对这个系统进行观测，这个向量会瞬间随机地跳变到红色、黄色或绿色轴中的某一条上。

sents.en: The more aligned it is with one axis, the more likely it is to snap to that axis instead of the others, but its fate is ultimately unpredictable. Let’s say it goes green.
sents.zh: 它与某条轴越对齐，就越有可能跳变到那条轴而不是其他轴，但它的最终归宿是不可预测的。假设它跳到了绿色。

sents.en: You’ll observe a green light, and there is now a 100% chance that it will still be green in subsequent measurements, because the arrow is fully aligned with the green axis.
sents.zh: 你会观测到绿光，并且此后再测量它仍是绿色的概率为100%，因为这个箭头已经完全与绿色轴对齐。

sents.en: The quantum superposition is no more.
sents.zh: 量子叠加态不复存在。

paragraphs.en: The more possible futures an object has, the bigger its Hilbert space. A coinlike particle with two possible futures is a “qubit,” the computational building block of quantum computers. It has a two-dimensional Hilbert space. Our three-color traffic light has a three-dimensional Hilbert space. But that’s just the beginning. A freely floating particle could be found in any location in the universe, so its Hilbert space must span an infinite number of dimensions.
paragraphs.zh: 一个对象可能拥有的未来越多，它的希尔伯特空间就越大。 一个具有两种可能未来的硬币状粒子是一个“量子比特”，即量子计算机的计算基本单元。 它有一个二维的希尔伯特空间。 我们的三色交通灯有一个三维的希尔伯特空间。 但这仅仅是开始。 一个自由漂浮的粒子可能出现在宇宙中的任何位置，因此它的希尔伯特空间必须跨越无限多个维度。

sents.en: The more possible futures an object has, the bigger its Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 一个对象可能拥有的未来越多，它的希尔伯特空间就越大。

sents.en: A coinlike particle with two possible futures is a “qubit,” the computational building block of quantum computers.
sents.zh: 一个具有两种可能未来的硬币状粒子是一个“量子比特”，即量子计算机的计算基本单元。

sents.en: It has a two-dimensional Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 它有一个二维的希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: Our three-color traffic light has a three-dimensional Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 我们的三色交通灯有一个三维的希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: But that’s just the beginning.
sents.zh: 但这仅仅是开始。

sents.en: A freely floating particle could be found in any location in the universe, so its Hilbert space must span an infinite number of dimensions.
sents.zh: 一个自由漂浮的粒子可能出现在宇宙中的任何位置，因此它的希尔伯特空间必须跨越无限多个维度。

paragraphs.en: This size — whether it’s two dimensions or an infinite number — is the only fundamental feature of a Hilbert space, according to von Neumann’s rules. The axes are arbitrary and imagined by us; they aren’t intrinsic to the space.
paragraphs.zh: 根据冯·诺依曼的规则，这个维数——无论是二维还是无穷维——是希尔伯特空间唯一的基本特征。 坐标轴是任意的，是由我们想象出来的；它们并不是空间所固有的。

sents.en: This size — whether it’s two dimensions or an infinite number — is the only fundamental feature of a Hilbert space, according to von Neumann’s rules.
sents.zh: 根据冯·诺依曼的规则，这个维数——无论是二维还是无穷维——是希尔伯特空间唯一的基本特征。

sents.en: The axes are arbitrary and imagined by us; they aren’t intrinsic to the space.
sents.zh: 坐标轴是任意的，是由我们想象出来的；它们并不是空间所固有的。

paragraphs.en: Consider an electron. It has one state, one arrow, pointing in a vast Hilbert space. Its Hilbert space spans all possible measurements — energy, position, momentum, etc. If you are curious where the electron might be, you can mark the space with the axes that represent possible positions. If you are wondering where the particle might be going, you apply a different set of axes, those representing possible momenta. No matter which measurement you intend to make, the underlying Hilbert space remains the same.
paragraphs.zh: 考虑一个电子。 它有一个态、一支箭头，指向广阔的希尔伯特空间。 它的希尔伯特空间涵盖所有可能的测量——能量、位置、动量等等。 如果你想知道电子可能在哪里，你可以在空间中标记代表可能位置的坐标轴。 如果你想知道粒子可能往哪儿去，你可以应用另一组坐标轴，即代表可能动量的那组轴。 无论你打算进行哪种测量，底层的希尔伯特空间都保持不变。

sents.en: Consider an electron.
sents.zh: 考虑一个电子。

sents.en: It has one state, one arrow, pointing in a vast Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 它有一个态、一支箭头，指向广阔的希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: Its Hilbert space spans all possible measurements — energy, position, momentum, etc.
sents.zh: 它的希尔伯特空间涵盖所有可能的测量——能量、位置、动量等等。

sents.en: If you are curious where the electron might be, you can mark the space with the axes that represent possible positions.
sents.zh: 如果你想知道电子可能在哪里，你可以在空间中标记代表可能位置的坐标轴。

sents.en: If you are wondering where the particle might be going, you apply a different set of axes, those representing possible momenta.
sents.zh: 如果你想知道粒子可能往哪儿去，你可以应用另一组坐标轴，即代表可能动量的那组轴。

sents.en: No matter which measurement you intend to make, the underlying Hilbert space remains the same.
sents.zh: 无论你打算进行哪种测量，底层的希尔伯特空间都保持不变。

paragraphs.en: This freedom to carve up Hilbert space as we see fit is what allowed Heisenberg and Schrödinger to come up with two distinct versions of the same theory. Heisenberg’s picture essentially put in axes and let them rotate around the vector, while Schrödinger’s picture did the opposite: It put in a fixed set of axes and let the vector rotate relative to them. They were two completely different mathematical perspectives on the same arrows, in the same Hilbert spaces.
paragraphs.zh: 这种随心所欲地划分希尔伯特空间的自由，正是海森堡和薛定谔能够提出同一理论的两种不同版本的原因。 海森堡的图像本质上是固定向量而让坐标轴绕其旋转，而薛定谔的图像则相反：它固定一组坐标轴，让向量相对于它们旋转。 它们是对相同的向量、在相同的希尔伯特空间中的两种截然不同的数学视角。

sents.en: This freedom to carve up Hilbert space as we see fit is what allowed Heisenberg and Schrödinger to come up with two distinct versions of the same theory.
sents.zh: 这种随心所欲地划分希尔伯特空间的自由，正是海森堡和薛定谔能够提出同一理论的两种不同版本的原因。

sents.en: Heisenberg’s picture essentially put in axes and let them rotate around the vector, while Schrödinger’s picture did the opposite: It put in a fixed set of axes and let the vector rotate relative to them.
sents.zh: 海森堡的图像本质上是固定向量而让坐标轴绕其旋转，而薛定谔的图像则相反：它固定一组坐标轴，让向量相对于它们旋转。

sents.en: They were two completely different mathematical perspectives on the same arrows, in the same Hilbert spaces.
sents.zh: 它们是对相同的向量、在相同的希尔伯特空间中的两种截然不同的数学视角。

paragraphs.en: John von Neumann developed an underlying structure for quantum mechanics that involves arrows moving inside an abstract Hilbert space.
paragraphs.zh: 约翰·冯·诺依曼为量子力学发展了一种底层结构，该结构涉及在抽象希尔伯特空间中运动的箭头。

paragraphs.en: In the first of his 1927 papers, von Neumann laid out two mathematical criteria that defined such a space. First, it had to be “complete.” It couldn’t be missing any regions or points. And second, you had to be able to calculate the alignment between a state and an axis, which you can visualize by imagining a light shining straight down onto an arrow so it casts a shadow on an axis. (The longer the shadow, the more aligned with that axis the arrow is.) The space had to allow for this operation, known as an inner product. Any space with these two features, no matter its size or origin, was a Hilbert space.
paragraphs.zh: 在冯·诺依曼1927年的第一篇论文中，他提出了定义这类空间的两条数学准则。 首先，这个空间必须是“完备的”，不能缺失任何区域或点。 其次，必须能够计算一个状态与一条轴之间的对齐程度，你可以想象一束光垂直照射到一支箭上，使它在一条轴上投下阴影，以此将这一概念可视化。 （阴影越长，箭与该轴的对齐程度就越高。）这个空间必须允许这种被称为内积的运算。 任何具备这两个特征的空间，无论其大小或来源如何，都是一个希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: In the first of his 1927 papers, von Neumann laid out two mathematical criteria that defined such a space.
sents.zh: 在冯·诺依曼1927年的第一篇论文中，他提出了定义这类空间的两条数学准则。

sents.en: First, it had to be “complete.” It couldn’t be missing any regions or points.
sents.zh: 首先，这个空间必须是“完备的”，不能缺失任何区域或点。

sents.en: And second, you had to be able to calculate the alignment between a state and an axis, which you can visualize by imagining a light shining straight down onto an arrow so it casts a shadow on an axis.
sents.zh: 其次，必须能够计算一个状态与一条轴之间的对齐程度，你可以想象一束光垂直照射到一支箭上，使它在一条轴上投下阴影，以此将这一概念可视化。

sents.en: (The longer the shadow, the more aligned with that axis the arrow is.) The space had to allow for this operation, known as an inner product.
sents.zh: （阴影越长，箭与该轴的对齐程度就越高。）这个空间必须允许这种被称为内积的运算。

sents.en: Any space with these two features, no matter its size or origin, was a Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 任何具备这两个特征的空间，无论其大小或来源如何，都是一个希尔伯特空间。

paragraphs.en: “This was a major step in creating what we call Hilbert space quantum mechanics,” said Miklós Rédei , a philosopher of physics at the London School of Economics. “It’s a beautiful example of how mathematical generalization or abstraction takes place.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是创建我们所说的希尔伯特空间量子力学过程中的重要一步，”伦敦政治经济学院的科学哲学学家米克洛什·雷代说，“这是一个数学推广或抽象化如何发生的绝佳范例。”

paragraphs.en: Von Neumann referred to these abstract spaces as Hilbert spaces because his mentor Hilbert had been the first mathematician to explore specific spaces with infinite dimensions in the early 1900s. Hilbert’s work had relied on those spaces being complete and having an inner product, but he didn’t think of them as examples of a more general class of spaces until his protégé grouped them together. The older mathematician may have been surprised to find his name attached to this new mathematical structure. “Dr. von Neumann, I am really curious to know what these Hilbert spaces are, after all,” Hilbert reportedly asked during a 1929 lecture.
paragraphs.zh: 冯·诺伊曼将这些抽象空间称为希尔伯特空间，因为他的导师希尔伯特是二十世纪初最早探索无限维具体空间的数学家。 希尔伯特的工作依赖于这些空间是完备的且具有内积，但在他的学生将这些空间归为一类之前，他并未将它们视为某一更广泛空间类别的实例。 这位年长的数学家或许会惊讶于自己的名字被冠以这种新的数学结构。据说在1929年的一次讲座中，希尔伯特问道：“冯·诺伊曼博士，我真的很想知道这些希尔伯特空间到底是什么。”

sents.en: Von Neumann referred to these abstract spaces as Hilbert spaces because his mentor Hilbert had been the first mathematician to explore specific spaces with infinite dimensions in the early 1900s.
sents.zh: 冯·诺伊曼将这些抽象空间称为希尔伯特空间，因为他的导师希尔伯特是二十世纪初最早探索无限维具体空间的数学家。

sents.en: Hilbert’s work had relied on those spaces being complete and having an inner product, but he didn’t think of them as examples of a more general class of spaces until his protégé grouped them together.
sents.zh: 希尔伯特的工作依赖于这些空间是完备的且具有内积，但在他的学生将这些空间归为一类之前，他并未将它们视为某一更广泛空间类别的实例。

sents.en: The older mathematician may have been surprised to find his name attached to this new mathematical structure. “Dr. von Neumann, I am really curious to know what these Hilbert spaces are, after all,” Hilbert reportedly asked during a 1929 lecture.
sents.zh: 这位年长的数学家或许会惊讶于自己的名字被冠以这种新的数学结构。据说在1929年的一次讲座中，希尔伯特问道：“冯·诺伊曼博士，我真的很想知道这些希尔伯特空间到底是什么。”

paragraphs.en: A century after the birth of quantum mechanics, the theory has left physicists in an awkward position. We live in a world where objects change position as they move through three dimensions of physical space. But our most fundamental theory takes place somewhere else, in von Neumann’s vast realm of possibilities. What does that imply about the reality of our world, or that of Hilbert space?
paragraphs.zh: 量子力学诞生一个世纪以来，这一理论让物理学家处于尴尬的境地。 我们生活的世界里，物体在三维物理空间中移动时会改变位置。 但我们最基础的理论却发生在别处——冯·诺依曼的浩瀚可能性领域之中。 这对我们世界的实在性，或希尔伯特空间的实在性，意味着什么？

sents.en: A century after the birth of quantum mechanics, the theory has left physicists in an awkward position.
sents.zh: 量子力学诞生一个世纪以来，这一理论让物理学家处于尴尬的境地。

sents.en: We live in a world where objects change position as they move through three dimensions of physical space.
sents.zh: 我们生活的世界里，物体在三维物理空间中移动时会改变位置。

sents.en: But our most fundamental theory takes place somewhere else, in von Neumann’s vast realm of possibilities.
sents.zh: 但我们最基础的理论却发生在别处——冯·诺依曼的浩瀚可能性领域之中。

sents.en: What does that imply about the reality of our world, or that of Hilbert space?
sents.zh: 这对我们世界的实在性，或希尔伯特空间的实在性，意味着什么？

paragraphs.en: In quantum physics, Hilbert spaces use complex numbers, which involve the imaginary number i , and negative regions. But von Neumann’s fourth commandment guarantees that the odds of any possibility will always come out as a real, positive number.
paragraphs.zh: 在量子物理学中，希尔伯特空间使用复数（涉及虚数 i）以及负数区域。 但冯·诺依曼的第四条戒律保证了任何可能性的概率总会得出一个实数、正数。

sents.en: In quantum physics, Hilbert spaces use complex numbers, which involve the imaginary number i , and negative regions.
sents.zh: 在量子物理学中，希尔伯特空间使用复数（涉及虚数 i）以及负数区域。

sents.en: But von Neumann’s fourth commandment guarantees that the odds of any possibility will always come out as a real, positive number.
sents.zh: 但冯·诺依曼的第四条戒律保证了任何可能性的概率总会得出一个实数、正数。

paragraphs.en: To Sean Carroll , a philosopher and physicist at Johns Hopkins University, the message is clear. If quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory of nature, then Hilbert space should be considered the fundamental theater of reality, he argued in a 2022 paper . One of his lines of research seeks to distill our familiar world from the disorienting Hilbert space that encapsulates all the ways the universe could possibly be.
paragraphs.zh: 对约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的哲学家兼物理学家肖恩·卡罗尔而言，其中的信息再清楚不过。 他曾在2022年的一篇论文中论证，如果量子力学是自然的基本理论，那么希尔伯特空间就应被视为现实的基本舞台。 他的研究方向之一，就是试图从那个囊括了宇宙所有可能存在方式的、令人眩晕的希尔伯特空间中，提炼出我们熟悉的世界。

sents.en: To Sean Carroll , a philosopher and physicist at Johns Hopkins University, the message is clear.
sents.zh: 对约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的哲学家兼物理学家肖恩·卡罗尔而言，其中的信息再清楚不过。

sents.en: If quantum mechanics is the fundamental theory of nature, then Hilbert space should be considered the fundamental theater of reality, he argued in a 2022 paper .
sents.zh: 他曾在2022年的一篇论文中论证，如果量子力学是自然的基本理论，那么希尔伯特空间就应被视为现实的基本舞台。

sents.en: One of his lines of research seeks to distill our familiar world from the disorienting Hilbert space that encapsulates all the ways the universe could possibly be.
sents.zh: 他的研究方向之一，就是试图从那个囊括了宇宙所有可能存在方式的、令人眩晕的希尔伯特空间中，提炼出我们熟悉的世界。

paragraphs.en: Other physicists take a more pragmatic stance. Jonathan Sorce , a physicist at Princeton University, says that Hilbert space is a handy mathematical construction that is remarkably useful for describing many quantum systems — but not all of them. He belongs to a community of researchers searching for a mathematical construction that can describe the fabric of space and time as a quantum object. Such a theory is a prerequisite for answering big questions such as what goes on at the heart of a black hole.
paragraphs.zh: 其他物理学家则采取更为务实的立场。 普林斯顿大学的物理学家乔纳森·索尔塞（Jonathan Sorce）表示，希尔伯特空间是一种便捷的数学构造，对于描述许多量子系统极为有用——但并非对所有系统都适用。 他属于一个研究群体，这些研究者正在寻找一种能够将时空结构作为量子对象来描述的数学构造。 这样的理论是回答诸如黑洞中心发生着什么等重大问题的先决条件。

sents.en: Other physicists take a more pragmatic stance.
sents.zh: 其他物理学家则采取更为务实的立场。

sents.en: Jonathan Sorce , a physicist at Princeton University, says that Hilbert space is a handy mathematical construction that is remarkably useful for describing many quantum systems — but not all of them.
sents.zh: 普林斯顿大学的物理学家乔纳森·索尔塞（Jonathan Sorce）表示，希尔伯特空间是一种便捷的数学构造，对于描述许多量子系统极为有用——但并非对所有系统都适用。

sents.en: He belongs to a community of researchers searching for a mathematical construction that can describe the fabric of space and time as a quantum object.
sents.zh: 他属于一个研究群体，这些研究者正在寻找一种能够将时空结构作为量子对象来描述的数学构造。

sents.en: Such a theory is a prerequisite for answering big questions such as what goes on at the heart of a black hole.
sents.zh: 这样的理论是回答诸如黑洞中心发生着什么等重大问题的先决条件。

paragraphs.en: Physicists asking these questions have recently focused on an even more abstract space that seems especially well suited for their purposes. This kind of space is made up of the things you could do to a Hilbert space, such as slicing it up in different ways or rotating one slice into another. In this arena, they have found that black holes seem a bit less mysterious .
paragraphs.zh: 提出这些问题的物理学家们近来把焦点投向了一个更为抽象的空间，这个空间似乎特别适合他们的研究目的。 这类空间由你可以对希尔伯特空间执行的操作构成，比如以不同的方式对它进行切分，或将一个切片旋转变为另一个切片。 在这个领域里，他们发现黑洞似乎不再那么神秘了。

sents.en: Physicists asking these questions have recently focused on an even more abstract space that seems especially well suited for their purposes.
sents.zh: 提出这些问题的物理学家们近来把焦点投向了一个更为抽象的空间，这个空间似乎特别适合他们的研究目的。

sents.en: This kind of space is made up of the things you could do to a Hilbert space, such as slicing it up in different ways or rotating one slice into another.
sents.zh: 这类空间由你可以对希尔伯特空间执行的操作构成，比如以不同的方式对它进行切分，或将一个切片旋转变为另一个切片。

sents.en: In this arena, they have found that black holes seem a bit less mysterious .
sents.zh: 在这个领域里，他们发现黑洞似乎不再那么神秘了。

paragraphs.en: This sort of über-space is known today as a von Neumann algebra. Von Neumann himself helped develop it as a potential remedy for some logical inconsistencies with Hilbert space that troubled him. “I would like to make a confession which may seem immoral: I do not believe in Hilbert space anymore,” he wrote in a 1935 letter while exploring the virtues of algebras.
paragraphs.zh: 这类超空间如今被称为冯·诺依曼代数。 冯·诺依曼本人也参与发展了这一理论，将其视为解决希尔伯特空间中某些令他困扰的逻辑不一致问题的潜在良方。“我想坦白一件看似不道德的事：我不再相信希尔伯特空间了，”他在1935年探索代数之优点时的一封信中这样写道。

sents.en: This sort of über-space is known today as a von Neumann algebra.
sents.zh: 这类超空间如今被称为冯·诺依曼代数。

sents.en: Von Neumann himself helped develop it as a potential remedy for some logical inconsistencies with Hilbert space that troubled him. “I would like to make a confession which may seem immoral: I do not believe in Hilbert space anymore,” he wrote in a 1935 letter while exploring the virtues of algebras.
sents.zh: 冯·诺依曼本人也参与发展了这一理论，将其视为解决希尔伯特空间中某些令他困扰的逻辑不一致问题的潜在良方。“我想坦白一件看似不道德的事：我不再相信希尔伯特空间了，”他在1935年探索代数之优点时的一封信中这样写道。

paragraphs.en: Sorce, for his part, doesn’t share von Neumann’s desire for one space to rule them all. He’s content to use whichever mathematical construction best suits the quantum object he’s studying. Often it’s a Hilbert space. Sometimes it’s a von Neumann algebra. And occasionally it might even be one of the many other spaces mathematicians have cooked up over the last century.
paragraphs.zh: 而索尔塞（Sorce）并不认同冯·诺依曼想要用单一空间统摄一切的愿望。 他满足于使用最适合他所研究的量子对象的任何数学构造。 通常那是希尔伯特空间。 有时那是冯·诺依曼代数。 偶尔甚至可能是数学家们在上个世纪构想出的许多其他空间之一。

sents.en: Sorce, for his part, doesn’t share von Neumann’s desire for one space to rule them all.
sents.zh: 而索尔塞（Sorce）并不认同冯·诺依曼想要用单一空间统摄一切的愿望。

sents.en: He’s content to use whichever mathematical construction best suits the quantum object he’s studying.
sents.zh: 他满足于使用最适合他所研究的量子对象的任何数学构造。

sents.en: Often it’s a Hilbert space.
sents.zh: 通常那是希尔伯特空间。

sents.en: Sometimes it’s a von Neumann algebra.
sents.zh: 有时那是冯·诺依曼代数。

sents.en: And occasionally it might even be one of the many other spaces mathematicians have cooked up over the last century.
sents.zh: 偶尔甚至可能是数学家们在上个世纪构想出的许多其他空间之一。

paragraphs.en: “There’s a whole zoo of these things,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “这些东西简直就像一个动物园，”他说。
